contentBlocks.text: This week you analyzed 'Why Our School Should Start a Community Garden' through three separate lenses: ethos, pathos, and logos. Today, bring it all together into one complete rhetorical analysis.

Quick review: ethos builds credibility through experience, expertise, and precedent (Day 2). Pathos appeals to emotion through specific, honest imagery (Day 3). Logos provides a logical if-then structure connecting evidence to a claim (Day 4). Effective persuasive writing weaves all three together, not just one. Write one paragraph analyzing how the garden speech uses all three appeals together, citing at least one specific example of each.
You just completed a real, complete rhetorical analysis — a genuinely sophisticated skill you'll use to evaluate speeches, ads, and essays for the rest of this course and beyond.

objectives: Recall the three rhetorical appeals: ethos, pathos, logos
Write a complete analysis identifying all three appeals with specific textual evidence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their combined analysis paragraph using their earlier worksheets.
3. Read the finished paragraph aloud together.
4. Celebrate finishing a real, complete rhetorical analysis — a genuinely advanced skill for this grade.
5. Note this same ethos/pathos/logos framework will apply to every future speech, ad, or persuasive essay studied this year.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the analysis to be organized as 3 clearly separate sentences (one per appeal) rather than requiring smooth blended prose
Ready for more: ask them to find a real speech or ad (with adult guidance) and identify its use of all three appeals
This is a genuine analytical-writing milestone — celebrate it as real rhetorical criticism, matching the course's own 'rhetoric' description
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary — check the paragraph addresses all 3 appeals (ethos, pathos, logos) with a specific example of each from the speech, not just definitions repeated without evidence.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Synthesizes the week's Common Core RI.9-10.6 rhetoric-analysis standard into one complete analytical piece, matching the course's own 'rhetoric' description end to end.
